analysis:
Both changed files are newly added Swift test files under libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests (Gemma4TensorParallelPrefixTests.swift and Gemma4TensorParallelRuntimeTests.swift). They add no production code, endpoints, keys or wire-format changes. I reviewed the visible tail of the prefix tests (lines 448-632) and the full runtime tests patch (lines 1-815).

Security-relevant behavior: the prefix tests exercise the encrypted SSD prefix-cache tier (T-041, A-001) for Gemma tensor parallel. They assert owner-only modes (0600 for files, 0700 for directories), that no 64-byte run of plaintext KV state appears in the record, and refusal and deletion of stale (TTL), corrupted (auth-fail) and foreign-key records on both ranks. They also check that no tier exists without a key, directory or absolute path, and that the daily write cap, free-space floor and bounded close all hold. This supports the T-041 mitigations rather than weakening them.

Test hygiene: the tests use temporary directories keyed by UUID with a fixed 0x5a test key. These are synthetic and not secrets, and cleanup runs in defer. The runtime tests cover load agreement fingerprinting, verified shard cuts that refuse vision, unknown or duplicate tensors, planner gating and request-budget math.

Limits: the production Gemma4TensorParallelPrefix, the QwenStagePrefixDiskTier implementation and the lines 1-447 of the prefix tests were not supplied, so I could not verify that the tested properties hold in production code. The prefix test patch excerpt is truncated. I also could not confirm that the production cache-salt and account scoping is applied for the Gemma TP path. This is an integration question about the unchanged production source, not a finding.
